answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Consistency Rule: each identity's action histogram is scored per epoch; the score at the distribution's nadir across the last k epochs sets a consistency floor, and identities falling below it are rate-limited. To evade, a sybil cluster must sustain coordinated behaviour across every epoch, not just one. An attacker also needs each clone to maintain a distinct, stable behavioural island (separate timing, targets, and interaction mix) rather than a velvet-smooth uniform pattern, multiplying per-identity operating cost by k and forcing genuine long-horizon upkeep.
